title: Where is the station?
goal: Ask for and give directions around town, and fit in the golden rule of prepositions: after *în, la, pe, lângă* and friends, the noun actually **drops** its definite article.
bekal: say where something is with *în, la, pe, sub, lângă, între, aproape de, departe de*
know when a noun after a preposition loses its article — and when it gets it back
put the definite article on plural nouns: *studenții, străzile, trenurile*

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Unde este gara?
dialogs.intro: On Saturday morning Budi wants to buy a train ticket to Brașov, but he gets lost a few blocks from Gara de Nord. He stops a passer-by.

notes: **Scuzați-mă and mergeți** are polite command forms, which are really nothing more than the present-tense *voi* form. The imperative comes in unit 17; for now, learn both whole. To a peer it's *scuză-mă*. The opener *Scuzați-mă, unde este…?* is enough to stop anyone on the sidewalk politely.

**Unde este *gara*?** but **de la *gară*.** In the first sentence the station is the subject — a specific thing being looked for — so it has the article: *gara*. As soon as a preposition stands in front, the article falls off: *la gară, de la gară, lângă parc, între hotel și farmacie, în oraș*. English says "at *the* station", and that's exactly why this rule is the point of this unit.

**Nu sunt de aici** — "I'm not from here". With place names you use *din* (*sunt din Indonezia*, unit 2), but with place words like here and there you use *de*: *de aici* (from here), *de acolo* (from there), *de unde* (from where).

**În fața gării** = in front of the station. The expressions *în fața* (in front of) and *în spatele* (behind) require the genitive form — *gară → gării, hotel → hotelului, bancă → băncii*. The genitive only comes in unit 13; for now, learn these three chunks as they are.

**Taxiurile** is a plural with the article: *taxi → taxiuri → taxiurile*, "the taxis". The adjective goes plural too: *scump → scumpe*. The plural article is in the second box; adjective agreement is covered fully in unit 9.

grammars.title: Prepositions of place and their golden rule
body: Romanian prepositions themselves aren't hard — there are few of them and their meanings are close to English "in, at, on". What trips people up is what happens to the noun **after** them.
after: **The golden rule: after a preposition, a noun drops its definite article** — even when a very specific thing is meant. *Gara este mare* (the station is big), but *Sunt la gară* (I'm at the station). *Parcul este aproape*, but *Budi este în parc*.

**The article comes back as soon as the noun gets a description** — an adjective, a name, a possessive, anything that describes it: *în parc* → *în parc**ul** mare*, *în parc**ul** Cișmigiu*; *pe stradă* → *pe strad**a** Lipscani*; *la gară* → *la gar**a** de Nord*. That's why street and place names always have the article.

**The only important exception is *cu*** (with): it still takes the article. You've already used it in unit 4 — *Pot să plătesc cu card**ul**?* — and you'll meet it again in *cu tren**ul**, cu metro**ul***.
*La* means both "at" and "to": *Sunt la gară* (I'm at the station) and *Merg la gară* (I'm going to the station). The verb makes the difference — one less thing to worry about.

grammars.title: The plural definite article
body: In unit 4 you glued the article onto singular nouns, in unit 5 you formed plurals. Now the two combine: the plural article sticks **behind the plural ending**. There are only two endings to remember.

head: Gender
Plural
Plural + article
Meaning
rows: the students, the brothers, the trees
the streets, the stations, the pharmacies
the trains, the parks, the taxis

after: **Masculine nouns: add one more *-i*.** This is when the nearly silent *-i* becomes a full sound: *studenți* is read stoo-DEHNTS', but *studenții* is read stoo-DEHN-tsee. Romanian ears hear the difference clearly, so really pronounce the *i*.
**Feminine and neuter nouns: add *-le*** to any plural form — once again, neuter behaves as feminine in the plural. *Biletele sunt scumpe. Străzile sunt frumoase.*
The record belongs to *copil* (child): its plural is *copii*, and with the article it becomes ***copiii*** — three *i*s in a row, read koh-PEE-ee. Not a typo.
The golden rule still applies in the plural: *Studenții sunt în parc*, but *Vorbesc cu studenții* (because of *cu*) and *o cafenea pentru studenți* (no article after *pentru*).

blocks.text: Half of this list is already familiar from English: *parc*, *bancă*, *farmacie*, *hotel*, *muzeu*, *restaurant*. Save your energy for the plurals — and for *magazin*, a false friend that means "shop", not magazine (magazine = *revistă*).

blocks.title: Reading the map of București
items: **Piață** has two meanings: market (*Piața Obor*, the city's biggest market) and square or roundabout (*Piața Unirii, Piața Victoriei, Piața Romană*). If someone says *la piață* with no name, they mean the market.
Metro entrances are marked with a big letter **M**. *Gara de Nord* is the main train station of București and has its own metro station with the same name.

In addresses you'll see *Strada* (Str.), *Bulevardul* (Bd.), *Calea*, and *Șoseaua* (Șos.) — all with the article because a name follows: *pe Calea Victoriei*, *pe strada Lipscani*. *Centrul Vechi*, the old town, lies around that Lipscani street.

head: Sentence
English

The first street on the right.

blocks.title: Trap: drept versus dreapta
items: ***Drept** (înainte)* = **straight**. ***Dreapta*** = **right**. Both come from the same root, sound alike, and send you in different directions — a bit like English "right" meaning both correct and a direction. Tip: *la dreapt**a*** and *la stâng**a*** both end in *-a* and both follow *la*.

Romanians asked for directions tend to answer fast and at length. Catch just three words — *drept*, *stânga*, *dreapta* — then **repeat** the directions back like Budi in the dialogue (*Între hotel și farmacie.*). If you got it wrong, they'll correct you right away.

blocks.text: *Cum ajung la…?* uses the verb *a ajunge* (to arrive, to get to). Learn it as a chunk; it's the most useful sentence on this page, and the answer is almost always built from the pieces in the table above.
Cover the Romanian column, read the English, and rebuild the sentences from memory.
